```{r setup, include=FALSE}
## FluMoDL was pulled from live CRAN and now lives only in the Archive. A bare

    if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")

                          quiet = TRUE)
```

```{r parallel-setup, include=FALSE}
## ---- guarded parallel backend (v6, current best-practice as of 2026) ------
## The diag-loco-dlnm chunk below (12 near-full-size model refits, one per
## excluded centre) is embarrassingly parallel -- N independent calls to
## run_dlnm_spec() with no shared state -- and was the actual source of the
## delay reported ("stacks a lot from diag-mmt-simultaneous-band onward"),
## not the MMT bootstrap chunk itself (that's already the fast Monte Carlo
## version, no refitting).
##
## Backend selection, in order of preference:
##   1. mirai (via future.mirai) -- the current recommended future backend.
##      Unlike multisession, it doesn't rely on one R connection per worker
##      (so no 125-worker ceiling), has lower per-task overhead, and is a
##      drop-in plan() swap: furrr::future_map() code doesn't change at all,
##      it just runs on a faster backend underneath.
##   2. future::multisession -- universally available (ships via the base
##      `parallel` package), the safe fallback if future.mirai isn't
##      installed. Spins up FRESH R sessions that do NOT inherit already-
##      attached packages, so workers get an explicit package list below.
##   3. Sequential purrr::map() with a warning, if furrr/future aren't
##      installed at all -- slower, but the document still runs to
##      completion rather than failing outright.
##
## multisession (and, to a lesser extent, mirai's local workers) copy
## `dat`/`analysis_ready_matrix` to every worker process -- with a large
## pooled dataset and many workers, watch memory; reduce `workers` if needed.
furrr_ok <- requireNamespace("furrr", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE)
mirai_backend_ok <- furrr_ok && requireNamespace("future.mirai", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("mirai", quietly = TRUE)

if (mirai_backend_ok) {
  library(furrr)
  future::plan(future.mirai::mirai_multisession, workers = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1))
  message("Parallel backend: mirai (via future.mirai) -- ", max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1), " workers.")
} else if (furrr_ok) {
  library(furrr)
  future::plan(future::multisession, workers = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1))
  message("Parallel backend: future::multisession -- ", max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1), " workers. ",
          'Install install.packages(c("future.mirai","mirai")) for a faster backend.')
} else {
  warning("furrr/future not installed -- diag-loco-dlnm will run sequentially ",
          "(slower, but still correct). Install with ",
          'install.packages(c("furrr","future")) for a large speedup, or ',
          'install.packages(c("furrr","future","future.mirai","mirai")) for the fastest option.')
}

parallel_map <- function(.x, .f, ...) {
  if (furrr_ok) {
    furrr::future_map(.x, .f, ...,
                       .options = furrr::furrr_options(seed = TRUE,
                                                         packages = c("dlnm", "gnm", "dplyr", "tibble", "purrr", "rlang")))
  } else {
    purrr::map(.x, .f, ...)
  }
}
```

# Section 0. Shared helper functions

Every model fit, diagnostic, and plot in this document goes through exactly
one of these functions.

```{r helpers-fit}
## ---- lag basis -------------------------------------------------------------
build_lag_basis <- function(max_lag, lag_df = NULL, lag_knots = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(lag_knots)) return(list(fun = "ns", knots = lag_knots))
  if (!is.null(lag_df))    return(list(fun = "ns", df = lag_df))
  if (max_lag <= 3)  return(list(fun = "integer"))
  if (max_lag <= 14) return(list(fun = "ns", df = 3))
  list(fun = "ns", knots = logknots(max_lag, nk = 3))
}

## ---- quasi-AIC (Gasparrini/Armstrong convention) --------------------------
compute_qaic <- function(fit) {
  phi    <- summary(fit)$dispersion
  loglik <- sum(dpois(fit$y, fit$fitted.values, log = TRUE))
  edf    <- length(coef(fit))          # stratum eliminated, so this is cb params only
  -2 * loglik + 2 * edf * phi
}

## ---- one metrics tibble per fitted model -----------------------------------
## v4.2: added `max_RR` -- the peak predicted RR anywhere across the fitted
## exposure range, BEFORE centering. A cold- or heat-tail spline blowing up
## to RR=50-100+ (as opposed to the RR of ~2-8 typically seen even at extreme
## percentiles in DLNM mortality studies) is the signature of overfitting/
## extrapolation into a data-sparse tail, not a real effect -- and neither
## kappa nor dispersion reliably catches it (both can look fine while the
## curve is doing something implausible). Consumed by apply_decision_rule()'s
## new plausibility gate below.
compute_model_metrics <- function(fit, cb, MMT, max_lag, exposure_df, lag_df, max_RR = NA_real_) {
  rank_cb <- qr(cb)$rank
  tibble(
    max_lag = max_lag, exposure_df = exposure_df, lag_df = lag_df,
    converged  = isTRUE(fit$converged),
    dispersion = summary(fit)$dispersion,
    QAIC       = compute_qaic(fit),
    logLik     = sum(dpois(fit$y, fit$fitted.values, log = TRUE)),
    rank = rank_cb, n_basis = ncol(cb), full_rank = rank_cb == ncol(cb),
    kappa = tryCatch(kappa(cb), error = function(e) NA_real_),
    MMT = round(MMT, 2),
    max_RR = round(max_RR, 1)
  )
}

## ---- fit ANY (max_lag, exposure basis, lag basis) combination -------------
run_dlnm_spec <- function(data, max_lag, exposure_df = NULL, lag_df = NULL,
                           var_knots = NULL, lag_knots = NULL,
                           exposure_var = EXPOSURE_VAR, outcome_var = OUTCOME_VAR,
                           stratum_var = STRATUM_VAR, lag_prefix = LAG_PREFIX,
                           mmt_probs = MMT_SEARCH_RANGE, by = 0.1, cen = NULL, quiet = TRUE) {

  lag_cols <- paste0(lag_prefix, 0:max_lag)
  missing_cols <- setdiff(lag_cols, names(data))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    warning("Missing lag columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")); return(NULL)
  }

  lag_matrix <- as.matrix(data[, lag_cols])
  keep <- complete.cases(lag_matrix)
  dat  <- data[keep, ]; lag_matrix <- lag_matrix[keep, ]
  if (nrow(dat) == 0) { warning("No complete lag histories."); return(NULL) }
  if (!quiet) cat("max_lag=", max_lag, " rows=", nrow(dat), "\n")

  if (is.null(var_knots)) var_knots <- equalknots(dat[[exposure_var]], fun = "ns", df = exposure_df)
  lag_basis <- build_lag_basis(max_lag, lag_df, lag_knots)

  cb <- tryCatch(
    crossbasis(lag_matrix, lag = max_lag, argvar = list(fun = "ns", knots = var_knots), arglag = lag_basis),
    error = function(e) { message(e$message); NULL })
  if (is.null(cb)) return(NULL)

  fit <- tryCatch(
    gnm(as.formula(paste0(outcome_var, " ~ cb")), eliminate = factor(dat[[stratum_var]]),
        family = quasipoisson(), data = dat),
    error = function(e) { message(e$message); NULL })
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  q <- quantile(dat[[exposure_var]], mmt_probs, na.rm = TRUE)
  pred0 <- tryCatch(crosspred(cb, fit, by = by, model.link = "log"), error = function(e) NULL)
  MMT <- NA_real_
  max_RR <- NA_real_
  if (!is.null(pred0)) {
    idx <- pred0$predvar >= q[1] & pred0$predvar <= q[2]
    if (any(idx)) MMT <- pred0$predvar[idx][which.min(pred0$allRRfit[idx])]
    max_RR <- max(pred0$allRRfit, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  # Fallback: if no MMT could be located inside the search quantiles (rare),
  # centre at the median exposure rather than silently passing cen = NA into
  # crosspred() below -- keeps `pred` usable even when MMT itself is later
  # filtered out by apply_decision_rule()'s !is.na(MMT) gate.
  centre_value <- if (is.null(cen)) {
    if (is.na(MMT)) median(dat[[exposure_var]], na.rm = TRUE) else MMT
  } else cen
  pred <- tryCatch(crosspred(cb, fit, cen = centre_value, by = by, model.link = "log"),
                    error = function(e) pred0)

  list(data = dat, cb = cb, fit = fit, pred = pred, pred0 = pred0, MMT = MMT,
       centre_value = centre_value, var_knots = var_knots, lag_basis = lag_basis,
       metrics = compute_model_metrics(fit, cb, MMT, max_lag, exposure_df, lag_df, max_RR))
}
```

```{r helpers-selection}
## ---- hierarchical (sequential-gate) model selection ------------------------
## v7: tightened `max_rr_threshold` from 15 down to 2, based on this
## pipeline's OWN candidate diagnostics rather than a generic literature
## guess. The original default of 15 was calibrated defensively ("rarely
## above ~5-8") without reference to what this dataset's actual best
## candidates achieve -- and it was letting through models that are
## obviously overfit: Lag7_E5_L4/L3 (max_RR 56.4/53.9), Lag14_E5_L3/L4
## (~9.1-9.2), Lag7_E4_L3/L4 (~8.8-8.9), and several ~3.0-3.2 candidates, none
## of which belong on a shortlist for a UTCI-mortality DLNM. Meanwhile every
## max_lag in {21,28} candidate -- the ones with the best QAIC -- already
## sits at max_RR 1.0-1.3. A threshold of 2 costs nothing against the
## genuine best candidates and correctly excludes everything overfit,
## consistent with published DLNM heat-mortality RRs at extreme percentiles
## typically running ~1.1-2.5 rather than into the high single digits or
## beyond. Still a data-informed judgment call, not a universal constant --
## report whatever value you land on (and why) in the methods, and revisit
## if your MMT/exposure-df search space changes materially.
##
## v7.1: added `min_mmt_threshold` (default 25 degC UTCI), a SEPARATE gate
## from the existing `mmt_range` support check. `mmt_range` only asks "is
## MMT inside where we have data" (P5-P95) -- it says nothing about whether
## that value is physiologically plausible. An MMT of 16.5 degC passes
## mmt_range comfortably while still being implausible for a warm-adapted
## West African population, where the mortality minimum is expected near
## the upper-mid part of the local exposure distribution (commonly the
## 75th-90th percentile in MCC-network hot-climate sites), not near its
## cold edge. The two gates catch different failure modes -- keep them
## separate rather than folding one into the other.
##
## IMPORTANT CONSEQUENCE for the current 07 candidate grid: applying
## max_RR<=2 AND MMT>=25 together leaves only Lag14_E3_L3 and Lag14_E3_L4
## (MMT=28.8, max_RR=1.7) -- and both have QAIC ~274 units WORSE than the
## excluded Lag21_E5_L4 (142930.5). That's a real tension, not a rounding
## effect: the current grid does not contain a specification that is
## simultaneously well-fitting AND biologically plausible by both gates.
## Two honest ways to proceed once you see this reflected in your own
## decision$best_model:
##   1. Accept the plausibility-constrained winner even though it fits
##      measurably worse by QAIC -- a lower QAIC bought by fitting an
##      implausible cold-tail dip is not actually a "better" model.
##   2. Expand the Section 07 grid rather than choosing among what's here --
##      in particular, try quantile-placed knots (concentrated where the
##      data actually is, not equally spaced into the sparse cold tail) at
##      exposure_df=3-4, and/or add exposure_df=2 for max_lag in {21,28}.
##      This is exactly what the knot-placement sensitivity check (equal vs
##      quantile vs log) is for -- worth promoting from a post-hoc
##      sensitivity check into the primary candidate search if it turns up
##      a spec that satisfies both gates without the QAIC penalty.
## This function will not silently pick option 1 or 2 for you -- it applies
## the gates and returns whatever survives; the interpretation above is
## yours to act on.
apply_decision_rule <- function(metrics_tbl, mmt_range,
                                 kappa_max = KAPPA_MAX, dispersion_max = DISPERSION_MAX,
                                 qaic_tol = QAIC_TOLERANCE, max_rr_threshold = 2,
                                 min_mmt_threshold = 25) {

  # v7.1: per-candidate gate breakdown -- shows WHICH gate(s) each candidate
  # fails, not just a pass/fail count, so a tension like "the best-QAIC
  # candidates all fail min_mmt while the MMT-plausible ones fail max_RR" is
  # visible directly in the output instead of something you have to infer
  # by eye from a wide diagnostics table. Same principle as the centre
  # exclusion_report fix in two_stage_pool().
  gate_report <- metrics_tbl %>%
    mutate(
      row_id = if ("model_id" %in% names(metrics_tbl)) model_id else as.character(dplyr::row_number()),
      fail_convergence = !converged | !full_rank,
      fail_kappa       = !is.na(kappa) & kappa > kappa_max,
      fail_dispersion  = !is.na(dispersion) & dispersion > dispersion_max,
      fail_mmt_range   = is.na(MMT) | !between(MMT, mmt_range[1], mmt_range[2]),
      fail_max_rr      = !is.na(max_RR) & max_RR > max_rr_threshold,
      fail_min_mmt     = !is.na(MMT) & MMT < min_mmt_threshold,
      passed_all_gates = !fail_convergence & !fail_kappa & !fail_dispersion &
                          !fail_mmt_range & !fail_max_rr & !fail_min_mmt
    ) %>%
    select(row_id, max_lag, exposure_df, lag_df, MMT, max_RR, kappa, dispersion, QAIC,
           passed_all_gates, fail_convergence, fail_kappa, fail_dispersion,
           fail_mmt_range, fail_max_rr, fail_min_mmt) %>%
    arrange(desc(passed_all_gates), QAIC)

  candidates <- metrics_tbl %>%
    filter(converged, full_rank, !is.na(MMT),
           kappa <= kappa_max, dispersion <= dispersion_max,
           between(MMT, mmt_range[1], mmt_range[2]),
           is.na(max_RR) | max_RR <= max_rr_threshold,
           MMT >= min_mmt_threshold)
  if (nrow(candidates) == 0) {
    message("No candidate passed all gates -- printing the full gate_report for diagnosis before stopping.")
    print(gate_report %>% flextable() %>% autofit())
    stop("No candidate model passed the diagnostic gates (including max_RR <= ",
         max_rr_threshold, " and MMT >= ", min_mmt_threshold, "). See the gate_report ",
         "table printed just above for how close the best candidates came on EACH gate ",
         "separately, and consider expanding the candidate grid (e.g. quantile-placed ",
         "knots, lower exposure_df at long lags) rather than simply relaxing either threshold.")
  }

  best_LL <- max(candidates$logLik, na.rm = TRUE)
  candidates <- candidates %>% filter(logLik >= best_LL - 1e-6)

  best_QAIC <- min(candidates$QAIC, na.rm = TRUE)
  candidates <- candidates %>% filter(QAIC <= best_QAIC + qaic_tol) %>%
    arrange(exposure_df, lag_df, n_basis, kappa)

  list(best_model = candidates %>% slice(1), remaining_models = candidates, gate_report = gate_report)
}
```

```{r helpers-plots}
## ---- shared y-axis helper for cumulative RR curves -------------------------
## v4.2: base R's default axis on a curve spanning e.g. 1-70 produces coarse,
## far-apart ticks (0, 40, 80...) -- unreadable right where almost all the
## epidemiologically meaningful signal is, near RR=1. This returns fixed
## 0.5-unit ticks anchored to the RR=1 grid, with the visible range capped at
## `rr_cap` (default 10 -- comfortably above what a plausible DLNM mortality
## RR should reach; see the max_RR plausibility gate in Section 07) so one
## implausible tail spike doesn't dictate the scale for the whole curve. If
## the true curve exceeds the cap, that's reported (not silently hidden) via
## the `truncated`/`true_max` fields for the caller to annotate on the plot.
rr_axis_breaks <- function(pred, rr_cap = 10) {
  y_max_data <- max(pred$allRRhigh, na.rm = TRUE)
  y_min <- max(0, floor(min(pred$allRRlow, na.rm = TRUE) * 2) / 2)
  y_max <- ceiling(min(y_max_data, rr_cap) * 2) / 2
  list(ylim = c(y_min, y_max), breaks = seq(y_min, y_max, by = 0.5),
       truncated = y_max_data > rr_cap, true_max = y_max_data)
}

## ---- overlay cumulative RR curves -----------------------------------------
plot_curve_overlay <- function(results, labels = NULL, title = "",
                                xlab = "UTCI (\u00b0C)", ylab = "Cumulative Relative Risk",
                                show_mmt = TRUE, show_ci = FALSE, legend_pos = "topright") {
  keep <- !vapply(results, is.null, logical(1)); results <- results[keep]
  labels <- if (is.null(labels)) paste0("Model ", seq_along(results)) else labels[keep]
  if (length(results) == 0) stop("No valid models supplied.")

  cols <- grDevices::hcl.colors(length(results), palette = "Dark 3")
  x_rng <- range(unlist(lapply(results, \(x) x$pred$predvar)), na.rm = TRUE)
  y_rng <- range(unlist(lapply(results, \(x) if (show_ci) c(x$pred$allRRlow, x$pred$allRRhigh) else x$pred$allRRfit)), na.rm = TRUE)

  plot(NA, xlim = x_rng, ylim = y_rng, xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab, main = title, las = 1, bty = "l")
  grid(col = "grey90"); abline(h = 1, lty = 2, col = "grey40")

  for (i in seq_along(results)) {
    p <- results[[i]]$pred
    if (show_ci) polygon(c(p$predvar, rev(p$predvar)), c(p$allRRlow, rev(p$allRRhigh)),
                          col = adjustcolor(cols[i], alpha.f = .20), border = NA)
    lines(p$predvar, p$allRRfit, lwd = 2, col = cols[i])
    if (show_mmt && !is.null(results[[i]]$MMT) && !is.na(results[[i]]$MMT)) {
      rr <- approx(p$predvar, p$allRRfit, xout = results[[i]]$MMT)$y
      points(results[[i]]$MMT, rr, pch = 19, col = cols[i])
    }
  }
  legend(legend_pos, legend = labels, col = cols, lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = .8)
}

plot_candidate_models <- function(all_results, diagnostics_tbl, highlight_id = NULL, title = "Candidate DLNM Specifications") {
  labels <- paste0("Lag", diagnostics_tbl$max_lag, "_E", diagnostics_tbl$exposure_df, "_L", diagnostics_tbl$lag_df)
  if (!is.null(highlight_id)) labels[names(all_results) == highlight_id] <- paste0("* ", labels[names(all_results) == highlight_id], " (selected)")
  plot_curve_overlay(all_results, labels, title = title, show_ci = FALSE)
}

plot_lag_response <- function(pred, at, ci = "lines", title = NULL) {
  # BUGFIX (v4.2): dlnm::plot.crosspred(type="slices") requires `var` to
  # match a value in pred$predvar by EXACT floating-point equality, not
  # nearest-match. An arithmetic value like MMT - 5 essentially never lands
  # exactly on a `by=0.1` grid point, causing
  # "'var' must match values used for prediction" -- which value happens to
  # crash is just luck of the float, not a meaningful difference between
  # e.g. "Cold" and "Extreme heat". Snap to the nearest actual grid point.
  at_snapped <- pred$predvar[which.min(abs(pred$predvar - at))]
  plot(pred, "slices", var = at_snapped, ci = ci, xlab = "Lag (days)", ylab = "RR",
       main = title %||% paste0("Lag-response at UTCI = ", round(at_snapped, 1)))
}
plot_contour_surface <- function(pred, title = "Exposure-lag-response contour") {
  plot(pred, "contour", xlab = "UTCI (\u00b0C)", ylab = "Lag (days)", main = title, key.title = title("RR"))
}
plot_3d_surface <- function(pred, theta = 220, phi = 35, shade = .4, title = "3D exposure-lag-response surface") {
  plot(pred, theta = theta, phi = phi, shade = shade, col = "lightblue",
       xlab = "UTCI", ylab = "Lag (days)", zlab = "RR", main = title)
}

## ---- centre-specific curves, sorted to the geographic ordering ------------
plot_centre_curves <- function(fits, title = "Centre-specific exposure-response curves") {
  labels <- purrr::map_chr(fits, ~ {
    if (!is.null(.x$centre_label) && !is.na(.x$centre_label)) .x$centre_label else as.character(.x$centre_id)
  })
  ord <- order(match(labels, levels(centre_lookup$centre_label)))
  fits <- fits[ord]; labels <- labels[ord]

  cols <- grDevices::hcl.colors(length(fits), "Dark 3")
  x_rng <- range(unlist(lapply(fits, function(x) x$pred$predvar)), na.rm = TRUE)
  y_rng <- range(unlist(lapply(fits, function(x) x$pred$allRRfit)), na.rm = TRUE)

  plot(NA, xlim = x_rng, ylim = y_rng, xlab = "UTCI (\u00b0C)", ylab = "RR", main = title, bty = "l", las = 1)
  abline(h = 1, lty = 2, col = "grey50")
  for (i in seq_along(fits)) lines(fits[[i]]$pred$predvar, fits[[i]]$pred$allRRfit, col = cols[i], lwd = 2)
  legend("topright", legend = labels, col = cols, lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.6)
}

## Quick EXPLORATORY visual only -- re-pools centres by country independently
## of the main hierarchical model. For the publication-grade country estimate,
## use the Table 3 prediction from meta_reg_country in Section 10.2 instead.
plot_country_curves <- function(fits, cb, cen, title = "Country-pooled exposure-response curves (exploratory)") {
  countries <- unique(map_chr(fits, ~ .x$country %||% NA_character_))
  countries <- countries[!is.na(countries)]
  country_results <- map(countries, function(ctry) {
    sub_fits <- keep(fits, ~ identical(.x$country, ctry))
    if (length(sub_fits) == 0) return(NULL)
    if (length(sub_fits) == 1) return(list(pred = sub_fits[[1]]$pred, MMT = cen))
    coef_matrix <- do.call(rbind, map(sub_fits, ~ .x$reduced$coefficients))
    vcov_list   <- map(sub_fits, ~ .x$reduced$vcov)
    m <- tryCatch(mixmeta(coef_matrix, vcov_list, method = "reml"), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(m)) return(NULL)
    list(pred = crosspred(cb, coef = coef(m), vcov = vcov(m), model.link = "log", cen = cen, by = .1), MMT = cen)
  })
  names(country_results) <- countries
  country_results <- country_results[!sapply(country_results, is.null)]
  plot_curve_overlay(country_results, names(country_results), title = title, show_mmt = FALSE)
}

plot_meta_curve <- function(pooled_pred, mmt, rr_cap = 10, show_zones = TRUE) {
  ax <- rr_axis_breaks(pooled_pred, rr_cap = rr_cap)
  plot(pooled_pred, "overall", xlab = "UTCI (\u00b0C)", ylab = "Relative Risk", lwd = 3,
       ci.arg = list(col = "grey85"), main = "West Africa pooled exposure-response",
       ylim = ax$ylim, yaxt = "n")
  axis(2, at = ax$breaks, las = 1)

  # v5: Cold (below MMT) / Heat (above MMT) zone shading, same convention and
  # same rect()+rgb(alpha=) approach as diag-curve-slices. Exposed via
  # show_zones (default TRUE) rather than hardcoded, in case this function
  # is reused later for a comparison/overlay plot where the shading would
  # just be visual noise.
  if (show_zones) {
    usr <- par("usr")
    rect(usr[1], ax$ylim[1], mmt, ax$ylim[2], col = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.05), border = NA)
    rect(mmt, ax$ylim[1], usr[2], ax$ylim[2], col = rgb(1, 0, 0, 0.05), border = NA)
    label_y <- ax$ylim[1] + 0.92 * diff(ax$ylim)
    text(mean(c(usr[1], mmt)), label_y, "COLD", col = "blue", cex = 1.1, font = 2)
    text(mean(c(mmt, usr[2])), label_y, "HEAT", col = "red", cex = 1.1, font = 2)
  }

  abline(v = mmt, lty = 2, col = "red")
  if (ax$truncated) mtext(paste0("Curve exceeds axis cap of ", max(ax$breaks),
                                  " (true max RR = ", round(ax$true_max, 1), ")"),
                           side = 3, line = 0.3, cex = 0.75, col = "firebrick")
}

forest_plot_mixmeta <- function(fits, meta_fit, cb, at, cen, title = "Centre-specific cumulative RR") {
  eval_rr <- function(pred_fn) {
    pr <- pred_fn()
    idx <- which.min(abs(pr$predvar - at))
    tibble(RR = pr$allRRfit[idx], low = pr$allRRlow[idx], high = pr$allRRhigh[idx])
  }
  centre_df <- imap_dfr(fits, function(f, id) {
    lbl <- if (!is.null(f$centre_label) && !is.na(f$centre_label)) f$centre_label else id
    bind_cols(tibble(centre = lbl, country = f$country %||% NA_character_, deaths = f$n_deaths),
              eval_rr(function() crosspred(f$cb, f$fit, cen = cen, at = at)))
  })
  pooled_row <- bind_cols(tibble(centre = "Overall pooled", country = "", deaths = sum(centre_df$deaths)),
                           eval_rr(function() crosspred(cb, coef = coef(meta_fit), vcov = vcov(meta_fit),
                                                          model.link = "log", cen = cen, at = at)))
  df <- bind_rows(centre_df, pooled_row) %>%
    mutate(label = paste0(centre, " (n=", deaths, ")"), pooled = centre == "Overall pooled",
           label = factor(label, levels = rev(label)))

  ggplot(df, aes(RR, label, colour = pooled)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high), height = .18, linewidth = .6) +
    geom_point(size = 2.8) + scale_x_log10() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "black", `TRUE` = "firebrick"), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = paste0("Relative risk at UTCI=", round(at,1), " vs MMT=", round(cen,1)), y = NULL, title = title) +
    theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
                        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9))
}

## ---- Objective 2: lag-window ("harvesting") characterisation --------------
## Sums log(RR) across the lag days in each window at a stated exposure level.
## This is valid because the overall cumulative log-RR from crosspred() is
## itself just the sum of the lag-specific log-RRs in matRRfit.
summarize_lag_windows <- function(pred, at, max_lag, label = "") {
  idx <- which.min(abs(pred$predvar - at))
  log_rr_by_lag <- log(pred$matRRfit[idx, ])
  lag_days <- 0:(length(log_rr_by_lag) - 1)

  windows <- list(Immediate = c(0, 0), Short = c(1, 3), Medium = c(4, 7),
                   Delayed = c(8, min(14, max_lag)),
                   Harvesting = c(min(15, max_lag), max_lag))
  windows <- windows[!duplicated(map(windows, ~ paste(.x, collapse = "-")))]

  map_dfr(names(windows), function(w) {
    rng <- windows[[w]]
    sel <- lag_days >= rng[1] & lag_days <= rng[2]
    tibble(exposure_condition = label, window = w,
           lag_days = paste0(rng[1], "-", rng[2]),
           RR = round(exp(sum(log_rr_by_lag[sel], na.rm = TRUE)), 3))
  })
}
```

```{r helpers-centre-meta}
## ---- fit one centre with the FROZEN specification --------------------------
## BUGFIX (v6.1): every exclusion reason used to go through message(), which
## the global `knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE)` in `setup` silently
## swallows in the knitted output. That's exactly why "Fewer than two
## centres passed QC" was undebuggable -- the document had no way to show
## you WHICH centres failed or WHY (too few deaths? non-convergence? rank-
## deficient? kappa too high?) without you manually flipping message=TRUE
## and re-running. Fixed by returning the reason as DATA (a `reason` field
## on the return list) instead of a message -- two_stage_pool() below turns
## this into a table that's part of normal chunk output, which message=FALSE
## has no effect on.
fit_one_centre <- function(centre_data, centre_id, spec, var_knots, lag_knots, cen,
                            min_deaths = MIN_CENTRE_DEATHS, max_kappa = KAPPA_MAX) {
  fail <- function(reason) list(centre_id = centre_id, excluded = TRUE, reason = reason)

  n_deaths <- sum(centre_data[[OUTCOME_VAR]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_deaths < min_deaths) return(fail(paste0("too few deaths (", n_deaths, " < min_deaths=", min_deaths, ")")))

  # BUGFIX (v4): lag_df = spec$lag_df was previously omitted here, so
  # build_lag_basis() silently fell back to its own default instead of the
  # lag_df actually locked in Section 07. var_knots/lag_knots alone are not
  # enough to reproduce the locked spec when lag_knots is NULL (which it is
  # whenever Section 07 selected its lag basis via df rather than explicit
  # knots -- the normal case here, since the candidate grid always supplies
  # lag_df). This one argument is what silently decoupled every centre-level
  # model, and everything built on top of it, from the locked specification.
  res <- run_dlnm_spec(centre_data, max_lag = spec$max_lag, lag_df = spec$lag_df,
                        var_knots = var_knots, lag_knots = lag_knots, cen = cen, quiet = TRUE)
  if (is.null(res)) return(fail("run_dlnm_spec() returned NULL -- crossbasis or gnm fit failed (often too few rows/strata after complete.cases() on the lag columns for this centre)"))

  m <- res$metrics
  if (!m$converged)     return(fail("gnm did not converge"))
  if (!m$full_rank)     return(fail(paste0("rank-deficient crossbasis (rank ", m$rank, "/", m$n_basis, ") -- usually too few distinct exposure/lag combinations for this centre's data volume")))
  if (m$kappa > max_kappa) return(fail(paste0("excessive collinearity (kappa=", round(m$kappa, 0), " > max_kappa=", max_kappa, ")")))
  if (m$dispersion > 2) warning(centre_id, ": high dispersion (phi=", round(m$dispersion, 2), ") -- retained, not excluded")

  reduced <- tryCatch(crossreduce(res$cb, res$fit, cen = cen), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(reduced)) return(fail("crossreduce() failed"))

  pick1 <- function(col) if (col %in% names(centre_data)) unique(centre_data[[col]])[1] else NA_character_

  list(centre_id = centre_id, excluded = FALSE, reason = NA_character_,
       centre_name  = pick1("centre_name"),
       country      = pick1("country"),
       climate_zone = pick1("climate_zone"),
       centre_label = as.character(pick1("centre_label")),
       n_deaths = n_deaths, fit = res$fit, cb = res$cb, pred = res$pred,
       # BUGFIX (v4): store the actual filtered data used to fit this centre's
       # model directly, rather than relying on it being recoverable from
       # fit$data downstream (Objective 1's af_by_centre used to do this and
       # it's fragile -- not every model object is guaranteed to carry it).
       data = res$data,
       reduced = reduced, metrics = m, MMT = res$MMT)
}

## ---- Stage 1 (per-centre DLNM) + Stage 2 (mixmeta pooling) -----------------
two_stage_pool <- function(data, group_col = "centreid", spec, var_knots, lag_knots, cen,
                            min_deaths = MIN_CENTRE_DEATHS, max_kappa = KAPPA_MAX) {
  groups <- split(data, data[[group_col]])
  raw_fits <- imap(groups, ~ fit_one_centre(.x, .y, spec, var_knots, lag_knots, cen, min_deaths, max_kappa))

  # BUGFIX (v6.1): this table IS the fix -- it's ordinary chunk output (a
  # flextable, printed and returned to Results/), not a message(), so it
  # shows up in the knitted document regardless of the global
  # message = FALSE option. Every centre appears exactly once with either
  # "OK" or the specific reason it was dropped.
  exclusion_report <- imap_dfr(raw_fits, function(x, id) {
    n_deaths_seen <- sum(groups[[id]][[OUTCOME_VAR]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
    tibble(centreid = id, n_deaths = n_deaths_seen,
           status = if (isTRUE(x$excluded)) "EXCLUDED" else "OK",
           reason = if (isTRUE(x$excluded)) x$reason else "passed all gates")
  })
  print(exclusion_report %>% flextable() %>% autofit())
  write_csv(exclusion_report, "Results/CentreModels/Centre_Exclusion_Report.csv")

  fits <- raw_fits[!map_lgl(raw_fits, ~ isTRUE(.x$excluded))]

  qc_table <- imap_dfr(fits, function(x, id) {
    tibble(centreid = id, centre_name = x$centre_name, country = x$country,
           climate_zone = x$climate_zone, deaths = x$n_deaths, kappa = x$metrics$kappa,
           dispersion = x$metrics$dispersion, QAIC = x$metrics$QAIC, MMT = x$MMT)
  })

  if (length(fits) < 2) {
    stop("Fewer than two centres passed QC -- cannot meta-analyse. See the ",
         "exclusion report printed just above (and saved to ",
         "Results/CentreModels/Centre_Exclusion_Report.csv) for exactly ",
         "which centres failed and why.")
  }
  message(length(fits), " centres retained for meta-analysis.")

  coef_list <- map(fits, ~ .x$reduced$coefficients)
  vcov_list <- map(fits, ~ .x$reduced$vcov)

  # BUGFIX (v4): a dimension mismatch between centres' reduced coefficient
  # vectors would previously surface only as a cryptic rbind()/mixmeta()
  # error (or worse, silently recycle). Check explicitly and name the culprit.
  lens <- map_int(coef_list, length)
  if (length(unique(lens)) > 1) {
    bad <- names(coef_list)[lens != names(sort(table(lens), decreasing = TRUE))[1]]
    stop("Centre(s) with mismatched crossbasis dimension, cannot pool: ",
         paste(bad, collapse = ", "),
         " -- check that every centre received the same locked spec (max_lag/exposure_df/lag_df).")
  }

  coef_matrix <- do.call(rbind, coef_list)
  meta_fit <- mixmeta(coef_matrix, vcov_list, method = "reml")

  list(fits = fits, qc = qc_table, exclusion_report = exclusion_report,
       coef_list = coef_list, vcov_list = vcov_list,
       coef_matrix = coef_matrix, meta_fit = meta_fit, n_groups = length(fits))
}

heterogeneity_summary <- function(meta_fit) {
  s <- summary(meta_fit)
  Q <- s$qstat$Q; df <- s$qstat$df; p <- s$qstat$pvalue
  I2 <- max(0, (Q - df) / Q) * 100
  tau2 <- mean(diag(meta_fit$Psi))
  tibble(n_groups = meta_fit$nobs, Q = round(Q,2), df = df, p_value = signif(p,3),
         I2 = round(I2,1), tau2 = round(tau2,5), logLik = round(as.numeric(logLik(meta_fit)),2),
         AIC = round(AIC(meta_fit),2), BIC = round(BIC(meta_fit),2),
         heterogeneity = case_when(I2 < 25 ~ "Low", I2 < 50 ~ "Moderate", I2 < 75 ~ "Substantial", TRUE ~ "Considerable"))
}

leave_one_out_meta <- function(coef_matrix, vcov_list) {
  n <- nrow(coef_matrix)
  map_dfr(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    f <- mixmeta(coef_matrix[-i, , drop = FALSE], vcov_list[-i], method = "reml")
    tibble(omitted = rownames(coef_matrix)[i], logLik = as.numeric(logLik(f)),
           AIC = AIC(f), tau2 = mean(diag(f$Psi)))
  })
}
```

# Section 07. Crossbasis selection (multi-criteria, sequential-gate framework)

```{r cb-candidates}
candidate_specs <- expand_grid(max_lag = c(7, 14, 21, 28), exposure_df = c(3, 4, 5), lag_df = c(3, 4))
candidate_specs <- candidate_specs %>% mutate(spec_id = paste0("Lag", max_lag, "_E", exposure_df, "_L", lag_df))

all_results <- candidate_specs %>%
  pmap(~ run_dlnm_spec(analysis_ready_matrix, max_lag = ..1, exposure_df = ..2, lag_df = ..3, quiet = TRUE))
names(all_results) <- candidate_specs$spec_id
```

```{r cb-diagnostics-table}
diagnostics_tbl <- imap_dfr(all_results, function(res, id) {
  if (is.null(res)) return(NULL)
  res$metrics %>% mutate(model_id = id)
})
diagnostics_tbl %>% arrange(QAIC) %>% flextable() %>% autofit()
```

```{r cb-heatmaps, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
ggplot(diagnostics_tbl, aes(factor(exposure_df), factor(lag_df), fill = QAIC)) +
  facet_wrap(~max_lag) + geom_tile(colour = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = round(QAIC,0)), size = 2.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() + labs(x = "Exposure df", y = "Lag df", title = "QAIC by lag window")

ggplot(diagnostics_tbl, aes(factor(exposure_df), factor(lag_df), fill = kappa)) +
  facet_wrap(~max_lag) + geom_tile(colour = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = round(kappa,0)), size = 2.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma") + labs(x = "Exposure df", y = "Lag df", title = "Condition number (>500 unstable)")

# v4.2: max_RR heatmap -- makes the tail-extrapolation plausibility gate as
# visible/auditable as kappa and QAIC already are. A cell that's fine on
# kappa/dispersion but has an implausibly large max_RR (see helpers-fit) is
# exactly the failure mode this catches.
ggplot(diagnostics_tbl, aes(factor(exposure_df), factor(lag_df), fill = max_RR)) +
  facet_wrap(~max_lag) + geom_tile(colour = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = round(max_RR,0)), size = 2.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno") + labs(x = "Exposure df", y = "Lag df",
                                                   title = "Peak predicted RR anywhere on the curve (>2 flagged as implausible extrapolation)")
```

```{r cb-decision}
# Defensive rebuild in case this chunk is ever run before cb-diagnostics-table
if (!exists("diagnostics_tbl") || is.null(diagnostics_tbl) || nrow(diagnostics_tbl) == 0) {
  diagnostics_tbl <- imap_dfr(all_results, function(res, id) {
    if (is.null(res)) return(NULL)
    res$metrics %>% mutate(model_id = id)
  })
}

mmt_range <- quantile(analysis_ready_matrix[[EXPOSURE_VAR]], c(.05, .95), na.rm = TRUE)
decision <- apply_decision_rule(diagnostics_tbl, mmt_range = mmt_range)

# v7.1: gate_report printed unconditionally (not just on failure) so the
# max_RR-vs-min_mmt tension flagged during pipeline review -- the
# best-QAIC candidates failing the MMT plausibility gate while the
# MMT-plausible candidates fail the max_RR gate -- is visible every time
# this chunk runs, not just when nothing survives.
decision$gate_report %>% flextable() %>% autofit()
decision$best_model %>% flextable() %>% autofit()
decision$remaining_models %>% flextable() %>% autofit()
```

If `decision$gate_report` shows the best-QAIC rows failing `fail_min_mmt` while the
rows with `MMT >= 25` fail `fail_max_rr`, that is the grid-adequacy problem flagged
during review, not a bug: the current max_lag/exposure_df/lag_df grid does not
contain a specification that is simultaneously well-fitting and biologically
plausible by both gates. `decision$best_model` will still be whatever survives
both gates -- check its QAIC against the excluded best-QAIC rows in
`decision$gate_report` before treating it as final, and consider expanding the
grid (quantile-placed knots, lower exposure_df at long lags) rather than
relaxing either threshold to make the tension disappear.

exposure_df=5 candidates are excluded at the kappa gate before QAIC is ever
consulted -- their MMT also collapses to an implausible value versus the
exposure_df=3/4 candidates, which is the overfitting signature, not a real
effect. The surviving, simplest specification is locked below.

```{r cb-lock}
## v7.2: explicit manual lock -- Lag14_E3_L3. Rationale: among candidates
## passing BOTH plausibility gates (max_RR<=2, MMT>=25 -- see helpers-
## selection), only Lag14_E3_L3 and Lag14_E3_L4 survive. Their QAIC is
## essentially tied (143,204.4 vs 143,205.4, well inside QAIC_TOLERANCE=2),
## so the tie-break falls to parsimony: L3 has lag_df=3 (9 params,
## kappa=97) vs L4's lag_df=4 (12 params, kappa=120) -- simpler model,
## lower condition number, near-identical fit. MMT=28.8 degC UTCI is
## physiologically plausible for this warm-adapted population; max_RR=1.7
## is a plausible mortality risk magnitude.
##
## This is deliberately left as an EXPLICIT override rather than just
## trusting decision$best_model, so the choice stays auditable if the
## candidate grid or gate thresholds change later -- but note it is not a
## departure from the automated rule: apply_decision_rule()'s own
## arrange(exposure_df, lag_df, n_basis, kappa) tie-break already prefers
## L3 over L4 once both plausibility gates are applied. The check below
## confirms that agreement rather than assuming it.
manual_override_id <- "Lag14_E3_L3"

if (!is.null(manual_override_id)) {
  stopifnot("manual_override_id not found in all_results" = manual_override_id %in% names(all_results))
  auto_id <- decision$best_model$model_id[1]
  if (identical(manual_override_id, auto_id)) {
    message("Manual selection (", manual_override_id, ") matches the automatic decision ",
            "under the current gates -- confirms the plausibility gates + QAIC tie-break ",
            "already converge on this spec independently of the manual choice.")
  } else {
    warning("Manual selection (", manual_override_id, ") DIFFERS from the automatic ",
            "decision (", auto_id, "). Confirm this is intentional -- a human judgment ",
            "call is overriding what the sequential gates + QAIC picked -- and document ",
            "the reason in the decision log / methods, not just in this comment.")
  }
  best_id <- manual_override_id
} else {
  best_id <- decision$best_model$model_id[1]
}

best_fit <- all_results[[best_id]]

best_spec <- list(max_lag = best_fit$metrics$max_lag, exposure_df = best_fit$metrics$exposure_df,
                   lag_df = best_fit$metrics$lag_df, var_knots = best_fit$var_knots,
                   lag_knots = best_fit$lag_basis$knots, MMT = best_fit$MMT, cen = best_fit$MMT)

saveRDS(best_spec, "Results/Objects/best_specification.rds")
saveRDS(best_fit,  "Results/Objects/best_model.rds")

plot_candidate_models(all_results, diagnostics_tbl, highlight_id = best_id)
```

```{r cb-surface, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
plot_contour_surface(best_fit$pred, title = paste0("Locked model: ", best_id))
```

```{r diag-mmt-bootstrap}
## ---- v4: replaced 1000x data-resample-and-refit with Monte Carlo simulation
## from the fitted coefficients' sampling distribution. This is the standard
## approach for CIs on a *derived* nonlinear quantity from a DLNM (the same
## mechanism attrdl(..., sim=TRUE) uses internally, and the same mechanism
## already used elsewhere in this document for the pooled meta-analytic
## curve via crosspred(cb, coef=, vcov=, ...)). No data resampling, no model
## refitting: just repeated evaluation of the already-fitted curve. Runs in
## seconds. It captures coefficient-sampling uncertainty conditional on the
## locked crossbasis spec -- which is what you want here, since spec
## uncertainty (knot placement, df) was already handled by the sequential-
## gate search in Section 07.
## v4.1: 10,000 draws (free -- each draw is a crosspred() evaluation, not a
## refit), sub-grid MMT via splinefun()+optimize() instead of which.min() on
## a by=0.1 grid, and a simultaneous confidence band built from the SAME
## draws used for the MMT distribution (no extra simulation cost).
mmt_mc_uncertainty <- function(fit, cb, exposure_data,
                                mmt_range = MMT_SEARCH_RANGE,
                                by = 0.1, nsim = 10000, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  b  <- coef(fit)     # crossbasis coefficients only (stratum nuisance params already eliminated)
  Vb <- vcov(fit)
  sim_coefs <- MASS::mvrnorm(nsim, mu = b, Sigma = Vb)

  q <- quantile(exposure_data, mmt_range, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Fixed prediction grid, shared across all draws, so curves are directly
  # comparable column-by-column (needed for the simultaneous band below).
  base_pred  <- crosspred(cb, coef = b, vcov = Vb, model.link = "log", by = by)
  predvar    <- base_pred$predvar
  in_range   <- predvar >= q[1] & predvar <= q[2]
  log_rr_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nsim, ncol = length(predvar))
  mmt_sim    <- rep(NA_real_, nsim)

  for (i in seq_len(nsim)) {
    pr <- tryCatch(crosspred(cb, coef = sim_coefs[i, ], vcov = Vb, model.link = "log", by = by),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(pr)) next
    log_rr_mat[i, ] <- log(pr$allRRfit)

    if (any(in_range)) {
      # Sub-grid MMT: spline-interpolate the log-RR curve within the search
      # range and optimize(), rather than reading off the by=0.1 grid.
      sf  <- splinefun(predvar[in_range], log_rr_mat[i, in_range], method = "natural")
      opt <- optimize(sf, interval = range(predvar[in_range]))
      mmt_sim[i] <- opt$minimum
    }
  }

  list(mmt = mmt_sim, predvar = predvar, log_rr_mat = log_rr_mat)
}

mc_out   <- mmt_mc_uncertainty(fit, cb, dat[[EXPOSURE_VAR]], nsim = 10000)
boot_mmt <- mc_out$mmt

tibble(N_sim = length(boot_mmt), Median_MMT = median(boot_mmt, na.rm = TRUE),
       CI_low = quantile(boot_mmt, .025, na.rm = TRUE), CI_high = quantile(boot_mmt, .975, na.rm = TRUE),
       N_failed = sum(is.na(boot_mmt))) %>%
  flextable() %>% autofit()
```

```{r diag-mmt-simultaneous-band, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
## Simultaneous confidence band from the same 10,000 draws above -- accounts
## for uncertainty across the WHOLE curve at once (the maximum deviation any
## single simulated curve makes from the central estimate, at the chosen
## coverage), which is a stricter and more defensible standard than the
## pointwise band already shown in `diag-curve-slices`. Method: for each
## draw, take the max absolute standardised deviation from the mean curve
## across all UTCI values; the band uses the (1-alpha) quantile of that
## per-draw maximum, applied uniformly across the curve (Ryan & Loftus-style
## sup-t band, same logic dlnm's own CI machinery is built on).
alpha <- 0.05
mean_log_rr <- colMeans(mc_out$log_rr_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_log_rr   <- apply(mc_out$log_rr_mat, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
z_scores    <- sweep(mc_out$log_rr_mat, 2, mean_log_rr, "-")
z_scores    <- sweep(z_scores, 2, sd_log_rr, "/")
max_abs_z   <- apply(abs(z_scores), 1, max, na.rm = TRUE)
crit_val    <- quantile(max_abs_z, 1 - alpha, na.rm = TRUE)

band_df <- tibble(
  UTCI = mc_out$predvar,
  RR_fit = exp(mean_log_rr),
  RR_simul_low  = exp(mean_log_rr - crit_val * sd_log_rr),
  RR_simul_high = exp(mean_log_rr + crit_val * sd_log_rr),
  RR_pointwise_low  = exp(mean_log_rr - qnorm(1 - alpha/2) * sd_log_rr),
  RR_pointwise_high = exp(mean_log_rr + qnorm(1 - alpha/2) * sd_log_rr)
)

ggplot(band_df, aes(UTCI, RR_fit)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = RR_simul_low, ymax = RR_simul_high), fill = "grey70", alpha = .5) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = RR_pointwise_low, ymax = RR_pointwise_high), fill = "steelblue", alpha = .35) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
  labs(title = "Cumulative RR: pointwise (blue) vs. 95% simultaneous (grey) bands",
       x = "UTCI (\u00b0C)", y = "Relative Risk")
#ggsave("Results/Diagnostics/MMT_Simultaneous_Band.png", width = 8, height = 6)
```
